purpose: determine whether the failed ABCD reverse-peeling smoke was caused by non-contractive Picard iteration rather than inability to numerically recover the known true ABC predecessor of the final D update
ground_truth_policy: generate ABC from the frozen base with A then B then C, apply D once, and require the resulting ABCD target to match the frozen endpoint hash exactly; ABC is used only to assess solver error and never to initialize or steer the solver
solver_randomness_rule: reset the D stage seed before every loss or gradient evaluation so line-search evaluations see the identical stochastic realization
solver_viability_requires_all: ABCD target endpoint hash exactly matches the frozen replay hash
inverse potential is monotonically non-increasing up to FP64 tolerance
final inverse residual norm is at most 1 percent of its initial value
final distance to true ABC is at most 1 percent of the initial target-to-ABC distance
forward reconstruction error from the recovered state is at most 1 percent of the initial inverse residual norm

interpretation.pass: Picard failure is a solver/contraction failure; freeze a new four-candidate Armijo smoke on the same spent ABCD history before any all-24 experiment
interpretation.fail: Do not keep tuning inverse solvers. Pivot from explicit inverse recovery toward forward reachable-set residual or Jacobian-conditioned mode scoring on spent data.

anti_tuning_rules: do not change line-search constants, stopping ratio, iteration budget, initialization, or pass thresholds after observing output
do not initialize from ABC or any K3 predecessor reference
do not evaluate A/B/C candidate inverses in this diagnostic
do not launch either all-24 protocol regardless of this diagnostic outcome
do not touch held-out confirmation codebooks
